extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare payment and quality program stakeholders, health policy commenters, and regulatory compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: A federal register proposed rule describing proposed payment and policy changes for the FY 2027 Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) and Long-Term Care Hospital Prospective Payment System (LTCH PPS), including quality measure adoptions, reporting requirements, model changes, and statutory authorities. The page summarizes proposals, program-specific changes, and statutory citations that govern payments and quality reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comments posting policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received before the close of the comment period are available for viewing by the public, including any personally identifiable or confidential business information that is included in a comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are posted on https://www.regulations.gov. CMS will not post public comments that make threats to individuals or institutions or suggest that the commenter will take actions to harm an individual. CMS encourages individuals not to submit duplicative comments but will post acceptable comments from multiple unique commenters even if the content is identical or nearly identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language summary availability
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(4), a plain language summary of this rule may be found at https://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary is provided to aid public understanding of the rule; citation to the statutory requirement for such a plain-language summary is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of IPPS and LTCH tables on CMS website
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPPS tables and LTCH PPS tables for this fiscal year proposed rule are available on the CMS website at specified URLs (IPPS and LTCH PPS index pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click the 'FY 2027 IPPS Proposed Rule Home Page' or 'Acute Inpatient—Files for Download' links; LTCH tables listed under Regulation Number CMS-1849-P. For access problems contact Michael Treitel (DAC@cms.hhs.gov). Readers are referred to section VI of the Addendum for details on the table contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt Advance Care Planning eCQM across programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to adopt the Advance Care Planning electronic clinical quality measure (eCQM) in the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting, PPS-Exempt Cancer Hospital (PCH) Quality Reporting, and Medicare Promoting Interoperability Programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption timing varies by program (e.g., begins for certain programs with FY 2030 payment determination/program year as specified elsewhere in rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify and adopt five risk-standardized mortality measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to adopt five modified claims-based, risk-standardized mortality measures in the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program and subsequently modify these measures in the Hospital Value-Based Purchasing Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five are: Hospital 30-Day, All-Cause, Risk-Standardized Mortality Rate Following AMI Hospitalization; Following Heart Failure Hospitalization; Following Pneumonia Hospitalization; Following COPD Hospitalization; and Following CABG Surgery. Timing: begin in Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting (FY 2028 payment determination) and later modify in VBP (FY 2032 program year) as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt HRRP Sepsis readmission measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to adopt the Hospital 30-Day, All-Cause, Risk-Standardized Readmission Rate Following Sepsis Hospitalization measure beginning with an early look for the FY 2028 program year, and use beginning with the FY 2029 program year for the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a program-specific quality measure to be used in HRRP performance assessment beginning with specified program years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting (HIQR) measure actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple proposals in the HIQR program: adopt three new measures; remove three measures; modify three current measures; adopt five modified mortality measures; change data reporting/submission requirements for eCQMs and a structural measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific HIQR proposals include: adopt Excess Days in Acute Care After Hospitalization for Diabetes (FY 2029), Advance Care Planning eCQM (FY 2030), and Hospital Harm-Postoperative Venous Thromboembolism eCQM (FY 2030); modify three claims-based Excess Days in Acute Care measures (AMI, HF, Pneumonia) starting FY 2028 payment determination; remove VTE-1 eCQM, VTE-2 eCQM, and STK-02 eCQM beginning FY 2030 payment determination; mandatory reporting proposals: Malnutrition Care Score eCQM (mandatory beginning FY 2030), Hospital Harm eCQMs mandatory after 2 years of self-selected reporting beginning FY 2030; update reporting for Maternal Morbidity Structural measure beginning FY 2028. Also includes RFIs on emergency room access/timeliness, Adult Community-Onset Sepsis SMR, and Birthing-Friendly Hospital designation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPS-Exempt Cancer Hospital (PCH) Quality Reporting actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for the PCH Quality Reporting Program: adopt two new measures and remove one measure; establish eCQM reporting/submission requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, propose adopting Advance Care Planning eCQM and Malnutrition Care Score eCQM beginning with FY 2030 program year, and removing COVID-19 Vaccination Coverage Among Healthcare Personnel (HCP COVID-19 Vaccination) measure beginning FY 2028. Also propose eCQM reporting/submission requirements for the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH Quality Reporting Program (LTCH QRP) changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove two measures beginning with the FY 2028 LTCH QRP, revise LTCH QRP data submission deadlines beginning with FY 2029, and solicit public comments on an RFI for future measure concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific measures to be removed and the revised deadlines are addressed in the LTCH QRP section; includes request for stakeholder input on future measure concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple proposed changes to the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program including revisions to CEHRT definition, removal of certain attestations and measures, modification/adoption of measures, and alignment with HIQR eCQMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically propose: revise definition of certified EHR technology (CEHRT) per ASTP/ONC proposals; remove attestations related to ONC Direct Review and ONC-Authorized Certification Body (ONC-ACB) Surveillance; remove Support Electronic Referral Loops by Sending Health Information and Receiving/Reconcilling measures; modify the Electronic Prior Authorization measure; adopt Unique Device Identifiers (UDIs) for Implantable Medical Devices measure within Public Health and Clinical Data Exchange objective; adopt two new eCQMs in alignment with HIQR; remove three eCQMs to align with HIQR removals. Timing and program-year applicability specified in program section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed TEAM model updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed updates to the Transforming Episode Accountability Model (TEAM) that would modify policies affecting episode category triggers, quality measure assessment, and construction of target prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals include: adding MS-DRGs to initiate a spinal fusion anchor hospitalization; clarifying quality measure performance periods for certain measures; using a rolling historical Composite Quality Score (CQS) baseline period for certain measures; adding an APC and MS-DRG update factor to target prices; using the full baseline period to construct the prospective normalization factor. Also solicits feedback on RFIs regarding ambulatory surgical center episodes and voluntary participation of hospitals with physician ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJR-X Model policy proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to expand Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement (CJR) into CJR-X nationally with multiple policy specifications governing participant accountability, quality measures, pricing, exclusions, and data sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key proposals: mandatory model for acute care hospitals (except TEAM participants and hospitals in Maryland) starting Oct 1, 2027; LEJR episode of care accountability through 90 days post-discharge; five quality measures and a composite quality score (CQS); regional risk-adjusted target prices with capped normalization and trend factors; pricing-specific policies for low-volume and high-duals hospitals; permit provider and beneficiary overlap; allow participant hospitals to have financial arrangements; waive certain Medicare Program requirements; permit beneficiary-identifiable and regionally aggregated data sharing; options for Alternative Payment Model (APM) participation. CMS cites evaluation results, stakeholder feedback, and care delivery pattern changes as bases for modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit unlawful discrimination by GME and NAH programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal that approved medical residency training programs and approved nursing and allied health education programs must not discriminate, or promote or encourage discrimination, on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or religion, including the use of those characteristics or intentional proxies as a selection criterion for employment, program participation, resource allocation, or similar activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also proposes similar requirements for accreditors; requirement is in addition to meeting other applicable program requirements. The preamble discusses this in sections V.F.2. and V.G.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for identifying new residency programs (90% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed modification to criteria for identifying new residency programs under 42 CFR 413.79(l): for a residency program to be considered new, at least 90 percent of the individual residents must not have previous experience training in another program in the same specialty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal includes exceptions for small residency programs, displaced residents, and residents admitted via a binding third-party matching program. Also proposes to no longer consider the previous employment of the program director or faculty when determining whether a program is genuinely new for cap-building purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment penalty for failure to submit measure data as specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory requirement that the Secretary must reduce the applicable percentage increase that would otherwise apply to the standardized amount applicable to a subsection (d) hospital for discharges in a fiscal year if the hospital does not submit data on measures in the form and manner, and at a time, specified by the Secretary (section 1886(b)(3)(B)(viii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory mechanism underlies HIQR and other program reporting requirements and can result in reductions to payment updates for noncompliance with data submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare Promoting Interoperability meaningful use CEHRT requirement and payment adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(b)(3)(B)(ix) establishes payment adjustments under the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program by requiring downward adjustments to the applicable percentage increase for eligible hospitals that do not successfully demonstrate meaningful use of CEHRT for an EHR reporting period; section 1886(n) establishes requirements for being treated as a meaningful EHR user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment adjustments began in FY 2015 (and FY 2022 for subsection (d) Puerto Rico hospitals); the rule proposes programmatic changes to measures and attestations related to CEHRT and meaningful use requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disproportionate Share Hospital (DSH) adjustment qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(5)(F) provides for additional Medicare IPPS payments to subsection (d) hospitals that serve a significantly disproportionate number of low-income patients; the section specifies methods under which a hospital may qualify for the DSH payment adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule summarizes that qualifying hospitals receive a percentage add-on payment applied to the DRG-adjusted base payment rate; section 1886(r) and Affordable Care Act amendments modify the DSH methodology and provide for uncompensated care payment calculations described in three factors in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Medical Education (IME) and GME payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals with approved graduate medical education (GME) programs are paid for the direct costs of GME under section 1886(h), and hospitals paid under IPPS with approved GME programs are paid for indirect costs of training residents (IME) under section 1886(d)(5)(B); section 1886(a)(4) specifies that costs of approved educational activities are excluded from operating costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IME is a percentage add-on that varies based on the ratio of residents to beds. The preamble explains how GME and IME payments interact with IPPS standard amounts and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: New technology/new services add-on payment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for new technology or medical service add-on payments, a new technology or medical service must demonstrate it is a substantial clinical improvement over technologies or services otherwise available, and that absent an add-on payment it would be inadequately paid under the regular DRG payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain transformative new devices and certain antimicrobial products may qualify under an alternative inpatient new technology add-on payment pathway by demonstrating inadequate payment under the regular DRG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlier payment eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals' costs for a case are evaluated to determine eligibility for an additional outlier payment to protect hospitals from large financial losses due to unusually expensive cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any eligible outlier payment is added to the DRG-adjusted base payment rate and other applicable adjustments (DSH, IME, new technology add-ons, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of hospitals and hospital units excluded from IPPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(1)(B) specifies categories excluded from IPPS: rehabilitation hospitals and units; LTCHs; psychiatric hospitals and units; children's hospitals; cancer hospitals; extended neoplastic disease care hospitals; hospitals located outside the 50 States, DC, and Puerto Rico (U.S. territories listed); and religious nonmedical health care institutions (RNHCIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded hospitals/units are paid under reasonable cost-based systems (subject to rate-of-increase ceilings) or other PPSs established by statute and regulation; references to applicable CFR parts provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH PPS site-neutral payment rate and dual-rate system
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(m)(6) and related statutes established site-neutral payment criteria under the LTCH PPS, creating a dual rate system beginning in FY 2016 where LTCHs are generally paid the site-neutral payment rate unless discharge meets patient criteria for LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 51005(b) amended section 1886(m)(6)(B) to reduce the IPPS comparable amount by 4.6 percent for FYs 2018 through 2027. Existing LTCH PPS regulations are in 42 CFR part 412, subpart O. Annual LTCH PPS updates are issued with IPPS updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical Access Hospital (CAH) payment basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Under sections 1814(l), 1820, and 1834(g), payments made to Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) for inpatient and outpatient services are generally based on 101 percent of reasonable cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable cost is determined under section 1861(v) and regulations at 42 CFR part 413; CAH status depends on statutory requirements (rural location, bed count, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole Community Hospital (SCH) and Medicare-dependent, small rural hospital (MDH) payment rules and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: SCHs may be paid the higher of a hospital-specific rate (based on certain base-year costs) or the IPPS Federal rate; SCH defined in section 1886(d)(5)(D)(iii) by distance or absence of other hospitals. MDH program rules provide higher payment under certain conditions through December 31, 2026; MDH defined by rural area, ≤100 beds, not SCH, and high percentage of Medicare discharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With section 6202 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act (CAA), 2026 extending the MDH program through Dec 31, 2026, MDH status will expire Jan 1, 2027 unless changed by law; the preamble summarizes the statutory definitions and payment consequences for SCHs and MDHs.
